deliverables: Performance optimization targeting 2x to 10x improvements in snapshot signing and memory profile and reduced L1 fees through on-chain contract optimization
Operational excellence including operator runbooks, simpler node configuration, observability and logging, and an improved TUI
Ecosystem support including production-user and integrator-requested features, Hydra Alliance facilitation, hackathons, and developer relations
Maintenance and developer experience work including CI, tooling, and technical debt reduction
Milestone-gated delivery with independent third-party assurance
request.recipient: Input Output Global / IO: Hydra, with Intersect providing administrative treasury governance
request.what: Fund four Hydra v2 workstreams: performance optimization, operational excellence, ecosystem support, and developer experience/maintenance for a feature-complete and hardened Hydra v2.

claims.claim: Hydra is described as the only production-grade or production-ready Layer 2 scaling solution on Cardano.
The proposal states that Hydra is already used by Delta DeFi, Masumi, Hydra Doom, Glacier Drop, Intersect voting infrastructure, VTech Labs, Blockfrost, and Midgard.
The proposal claims Hydra provides sub-second finality, near-zero or zero internal transaction fees, high throughput, and L1-anchored settlement guarantees.
The proposal claims Cardano L1 has over two hours of finality, approximately $0.17 payment transaction fees, and roughly 7 to 10 TPS, making high-performance use cases uncompetitive on L1 alone.
The proposal claims competing platforms offer 400ms to 2s finality, sub-cent fees, and 1,000 to 7,000+ TPS, causing builders to exclude Cardano at the selection stage.
The proposal claims a single Hydra Head processes up to 1,000+ TPS in payment benchmarks and that aggregate throughput scales close to linearly with additional independent Heads.
The proposal claims every Hydra Head opening, funding change, and closure creates L1 transactions and fees, and that applications may route some internal fees to the L1 treasury on settlement.
The proposal claims upcoming L1 upgrades such as Leios and Peras will improve Cardano but cannot provide the zero-fee, sub-second, high-throughput envelope required by high-performance applications.
The proposal requests ₳5,100,781 and says funding will be milestone-gated with independent third-party assurance and Intersect administrative treasury governance.
The proposal states provisional users under evaluation include Bodega Market, Atlas Defi, Wingriders, Houselink, European Public Network, and more.

summary: The document requests ₳5,100,781 for Hydra v2 hardening and adoption workstreams, presents Hydra as a mature Cardano L2 with live and prospective users, and argues it improves Cardano performance, adoption, and treasury-linked activity, but many high-materiality adoption, benchmark, market, and comparative claims are asserted without evidence in the anchor text.
